title: Trend for Average Annual Government Spending on Foreign Students over Past 10 Years
what_it_is: Trend for Average Annual Government Spending on Foreign Students over Past 10 Years

sections.label: Education system serves Singaporeans
sections.summary: The core objective of the education system is to serve Singaporeans, and no Singaporean is displaced from an IHL by an international student.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The first point is that the core objective of our education system is to serve the needs of Singaporeans and no Singaporean is ever displaced from an institute of higher learning (IHL) because of an international student.

sections.label: Education budget and international student spending
sections.summary: The $13 billion education budget is overwhelmingly spent on local students, financial aid is for Singapore Citizens only, and spending on international student scholarships fell about 50% over 10 years to around 1% of the budget, or $130 million a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The second point I want to make is that the education budget of about $13 billion every year is overwhelmingly spent on local students, to make education affordable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To answer the Member's question, such financial aid is for Singapore Citizens only.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Member also asked for the trend of annual Government spending on international students in terms of scholarships and tuition grants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This has fallen by about 50% over the last 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) recently stated in a reply to a written question by the Member that the total Government spending on scholarships for international students in our schools and universities comes up to around 1% of our annual education budget, or $130 million a year.

sections.label: Tuition grants for non-Singaporeans
sections.summary: Non-Singaporeans may apply for tuition grants, foreigners still pay about twice what Singaporeans pay, and total tuition grant spending comes to about $238 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But there are other students who are not Singaporeans studying in our system and they may apply for tuition grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, we can accord them a tuition grant, but bear in mind, Singaporeans pay around 25% of the total costs of a university place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Even after tuition grant, a foreigner will still pay about twice the amount of a Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Member asked for the amount spent on tuition grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, scholarship is $130 million, tuition grant will be about—the total, will come up to be about $238 million.

sections.label: No data on other governments
sections.summary: The speaker does not have numbers on how much other governments spend on foreign students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for whether we have numbers on how much other governments spend on foreign students, I am afraid I do not have that number.

sections.label: Unicorn company and Singaporean roots
sections.summary: A company is now a unicorn hiring a thousand people, and all three are now Singaporeans with roots here; studies on costs and benefits are welcome but in the right proportion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, his company is a unicorn that hires a thousand people, and all three of them are now Singaporeans and have sunk roots here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, I welcome any studies to measure the costs and benefits, but the benefits are clear, but do it in the right proportion.

sections.label: Calibrating foreign versus local student spending
sections.summary: The question was whether spending is calibrated and balanced, and the figure of about $230 million is about 1.8% of MOE's budget and maybe 0.3% of the national Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, my question was really understanding what is that spending and whether it is calibrated and whether it is the right balance point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I think, basically, every society has to find the right balance point on a question like "How much are you providing in spending for foreign students versus local students?" Now that the Ministry has provided this figure, which is nominally about $230 million, I think that comes to about 1.8% of MOE's budget, which is maybe about 0.3% of the total national Budget.

sections.label: Reciprocity in international student spending
sections.summary: The speaker says he would keep an open mind on the figure and balance point if other governments' spending is comparable and reciprocal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: If there is data on what other governments are doing, if the spending is comparable on the part of other governments so that there is reciprocity – we are doing our part as good global citizens – I would certainly keep an open mind to say that that figure and the balance point are the right ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, if I hear correctly, these are the Member’s position – the Member does not advocate a zero international student policy, he had no fundamental disagreement with our approach.

sections.label: Converting foreign students to net-fee payers
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister's view on converting more foreign students to net-fee payers, citing a pool of international talent to compete for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But I think, fundamentally, there has been no disagreement with the approach of MOE.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would just like to know what is the Minister's view on the prospects of converting more of these foreign students to net-fee payers because I think we can all agree that there is going to be a pool of international talent we need to compete for and we need to give them some inducement to come.

sections.label: Students already net-fee payers
sections.summary: The passage states that today, some of the students are already net-fee payers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, some of the students are already net-fee payers.
